title: Stories and Narratives
description: Menceritakan kejadian dan pengalaman dengan narrative tenses: past continuous untuk latar (background), past simple untuk kejadian utama, dan past perfect untuk kejadian yang terjadi lebih dulu. Kamu juga belajar story connectors dan kata sifat emosi.
objectives: Menggunakan past continuous untuk membangun latar cerita
Membentuk dan menggunakan past perfect untuk kejadian yang lebih dulu
Menggabungkan past simple, past continuous, dan past perfect dalam satu cerita
Menggunakan story connectors dan kata sifat emosi untuk membuat cerita lebih hidup

lessons.title: Setting the Scene: Past Continuous
lessons.summary: Memakai past continuous untuk menggambarkan latar cerita dan aksi yang sedang berlangsung ketika sesuatu terjadi.
objectives: Membentuk past continuous dengan was/were + V-ing
Membedakan latar cerita (past continuous) dan kejadian utama (past simple)
Menggunakan when dan while dengan tepat
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Membangun latar cerita
Di A2 kamu sudah belajar past continuous (*was/were + V-ing*) dan bedanya dengan past simple (*when/while*). Di B1 kita memakainya untuk **membangun suasana (background)** di awal cerita. Good storytellers describe the scene first: the weather, the place, and what people were doing. Then something happens.

### Form
| Subject | Positive | Negative | Question |
|---|---|---|---|
| I / he / she / it | was + V-ing | wasn't + V-ing | Was ... V-ing? |
| you / we / they | were + V-ing | weren't + V-ing | Were ... V-ing? |

### Background vs main event
- **Background** (past continuous): aksi yang sedang berlangsung, seperti "panggung" cerita. *It was raining. People were hurrying home.*
- **Main event** (past simple): aksi yang terjadi dan menggerakkan cerita. *Suddenly, a car stopped in front of me.*

Long action + short action: *I was walking along the beach when I found an old bottle.* *While we were having dinner, the lights went out.*

### When vs while
**While** biasanya diikuti past continuous (aksi panjang). **When** biasanya diikuti past simple (aksi pendek). The meaning is the same in these two sentences: *While I was cooking, the phone rang.* = *I was cooking when the phone rang.*

### State verbs
Kata kerja "keadaan" seperti *know, see, hear, want, like, believe, seem* biasanya tidak memakai -ing: *I saw a light* (bukan *I was seeing a light*). *She knew the answer* (bukan *She was knowing*).

### Contoh pembuka cerita
*It was a cold evening in Port Selwyn. The wind was blowing and the streetlights were shining on the wet road. I was waiting for the last bus, and an old man was singing quietly next to me.*

Perhatikan bahwa belum ada yang "terjadi" — semua kalimat adalah latar. The story really begins with the first past simple verb: *Then the bus arrived, but it didn't stop.* Teknik ini membuat pendengar bisa membayangkan suasana sebelum masuk ke kejadian utama.

lessons.title: The Past Perfect: Form and Use
lessons.summary: Membentuk past perfect (had + V3) dan memakainya untuk kejadian yang terjadi sebelum titik tertentu di masa lalu.
objectives: Membentuk past perfect positif, negatif, dan pertanyaan
Menggunakan past perfect untuk alasan dan pengalaman sebelum titik di masa lalu
Membedakan present perfect dan past perfect
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Apa itu past perfect?
Past perfect (*had + V3*) dipakai untuk aksi yang terjadi **sebelum** waktu tertentu di masa lalu. Think of it as "the past of the past". Dalam bahasa Indonesia sering diterjemahkan dengan *sudah/telah* dalam cerita masa lalu.

*When I arrived at the cinema, the film had started.* → Film mulai lebih dulu (aksi 1), lalu saya tiba (aksi 2).

### Form
Bentuknya sama untuk semua subject — mudah!

| | Form | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Positive | subject + had ('d) + V3 | *She had left.* / *She'd left.* |
| Negative | subject + hadn't + V3 | *We hadn't eaten.* |
| Question | Had + subject + V3? | *Had you met him before?* |
| Short answer | Yes, I had. / No, I hadn't. | |

Remember: **'d** can mean *had* or *would*. In a story, *I'd lost my keys* = *I had lost my keys* because a past participle follows.

### Past participles
V3 sama dengan yang kamu pakai di present perfect: *go → gone, see → seen, eat → eaten, forget → forgotten, leave → left, meet → met, lose → lost*.

### Common uses
1. **Explaining a reason** (alasan) di masa lalu: *I couldn't open the door because I had lost my keys.*
2. **Experience up to a past point**, sering dengan *never / ever / before*: *Before 2020, Sinta had never travelled by plane.* *Had you ever flown before that trip?*
3. **Already** dalam cerita: *When we got there, the shop had already closed.*

### Present perfect vs past perfect
| Present perfect | Past perfect |
|---|---|
| sampai **sekarang** | sampai **suatu titik di masa lalu** |
| *I have never seen snow.* | *I had never seen snow before I visited Mount Ardan.* |

The past perfect always needs a reference point in the past. Jangan memakai past perfect jika tidak ada titik waktu di masa lalu sebagai acuan; kalimat *I had visited Lombok.* terdengar tidak lengkap tanpa konteks seperti *before 2015* atau *when I met you*.

lessons.title: Past Perfect vs Past Simple
lessons.summary: Menunjukkan urutan kejadian di masa lalu dengan past perfect dan past simple, termasuk by the time, before, dan after.
objectives: Memilih past perfect untuk kejadian yang lebih dulu dan past simple untuk kejadian berikutnya
Menggunakan by the time, before, dan after dengan tense yang tepat
Memahami perbedaan makna when + past simple dan when + past perfect
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Urutan kejadian
Ketika dua aksi terjadi di masa lalu, kita memakai **past perfect** untuk aksi yang terjadi **lebih dulu** dan **past simple** untuk aksi yang terjadi kemudian. This helps the listener understand the order, especially when we don't tell the events in order.

### When: three different meanings
| Sentence | Meaning |
|---|---|
| *When Ana got home, her mother **cooked** dinner.* | Ana tiba → lalu ibu memasak |
| *When Ana got home, her mother **had cooked** dinner.* | Ibu sudah memasak → lalu Ana tiba (makanan siap) |
| *When Ana got home, her mother **was cooking** dinner.* | Ibu sedang memasak saat Ana tiba |

One small change of tense gives a completely different story!

### By the time
**By the time** + past simple, + past perfect = pada saat itu, aksi lain sudah selesai. *By the time the police arrived, the thief had escaped.* With *by the time*, the past perfect is almost always necessary for the earlier action.

### Before and after
Dengan **before** dan **after**, urutan sudah jelas dari kata itu sendiri, jadi past perfect boleh dipakai atau tidak:
- *After Nadia had finished her homework, she watched TV.* ✓
- *After Nadia finished her homework, she watched TV.* ✓

Both are correct. The past perfect simply emphasises that the first action was complete.

### Already, never, just
Adverb ini sering muncul dengan past perfect: *The train had already left. I had never met her before. They had just moved in.*

### Don't overuse it
Jika kamu menceritakan kejadian **berurutan** (first, then, after that), cukup pakai past simple: *I woke up, had breakfast and left the house.* Past perfect hanya diperlukan saat kamu "mundur" ke kejadian sebelumnya. Another common mistake is using the present perfect in a past story: *When I arrived, they **have** left* ✗ → *they **had** left* ✓.

lessons.title: Narrative Tenses Together
lessons.summary: Menggabungkan past simple, past continuous, dan past perfect untuk menceritakan kejadian secara jelas dan menarik.
objectives: Memilih tense yang tepat untuk latar, kejadian utama, dan kejadian sebelumnya
Menggabungkan ketiga tense dalam satu kalimat atau paragraf
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Tiga tense, satu cerita
Cerita yang baik dalam bahasa Inggris biasanya memakai tiga *narrative tenses* sekaligus. Each tense has a clear job:

| Tense | Fungsi | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Past continuous | latar / aksi yang sedang berlangsung | *It was raining and people were running for shelter.* |
| Past simple | kejadian utama, berurutan | *I opened my bag and looked for my umbrella.* |
| Past perfect | kejadian sebelumnya / alasan | *I had left it at the office.* |

### Contoh cerita
*Last Friday I **was driving** home from work. It **was getting** dark and the traffic **was moving** slowly. Suddenly the car **stopped**. I **checked** the engine, but then I **realised** the problem: I **had forgotten** to buy petrol that morning!*

Perhatikan alurnya: latar (past continuous) → kejadian utama (past simple) → penjelasan tentang sesuatu yang terjadi lebih dulu (past perfect).

### Timeline thinking
Bayangkan garis waktu. Ask yourself three questions for each verb:
1. Is this the scene or an action in progress? → **past continuous**
2. Is this the next thing that happened in the story? → **past simple**
3. Did this happen before the story time? → **past perfect**

### Typical problems
- Memakai past continuous untuk aksi pendek: *When I was arriving* ✗ → *When I arrived* ✓.
- Lupa past perfect untuk kejadian sebelumnya: *My plane already left* ✗ → *My plane had already left* ✓.
- Berpindah ke present tense di tengah cerita lampau: *Then he says...* — in your written stories, stay in the past: *Then he said...*

### Mixing in one sentence
You can use all three in one sentence: *When I **arrived**, my friends **were dancing** — they **had started** the party without me!* Kalimat seperti ini menunjukkan kemampuan level B1 yang kuat. Jangan takut membuat kalimat panjang, asalkan setiap kata kerja punya fungsi yang jelas pada garis waktu.

mistakes.wrong: When I was arriving at the airport, my plane already left.

mistakes.wrong: I was so tired because I have worked all day.

mistakes.why: Alasan yang terjadi lebih dulu dalam cerita masa lalu memakai past perfect (had), bukan present perfect (have).

sections.summary: In a story, use the **past continuous** for background, the **past simple** for main events, and the **past perfect** for earlier events. lessons.title: Telling a Good Story
lessons.summary: Membuat cerita lebih hidup dengan story connectors (suddenly, luckily, eventually) dan kata sifat emosi (relieved, embarrassed, terrified).
objectives: Menggunakan story connectors untuk mengatur alur cerita
Menggunakan kata sifat emosi dengan tepat (-ed vs -ing)
Merespons cerita orang lain dengan ungkapan yang natural
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi, coba latihan berbicara, dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Struktur cerita
Cerita yang menarik biasanya punya tiga bagian: **beginning** (latar: who, where, when), **middle** (masalah atau kejadian tak terduga), dan **end** (penyelesaian dan perasaan). Use narrative tenses for the actions and connectors to guide your listener through the story.

### Story connectors
| Connector | Fungsi | Example |
|---|---|---|
| suddenly / all of a sudden | sesuatu yang tak terduga | *Suddenly, the lights went out.* |
| luckily / fortunately | kabar baik | *Luckily, nobody was hurt.* |
| unfortunately | kabar buruk | *Unfortunately, the last bus had already left.* |
| meanwhile | sementara itu | *Meanwhile, my brother was waiting at the station.* |
| eventually | akhirnya (setelah lama/usaha) | *We eventually found the hotel at midnight.* |
| in the end | pada akhirnya (hasil akhir) | *In the end, everything was fine.* |

### Emotion adjectives
Berikan warna pada cerita dengan menyebut perasaan. Use strong adjectives instead of only *happy* or *sad*:
- **relieved** — lega (setelah khawatir)
- **embarrassed** — malu
- **terrified** — sangat takut
- **amazed** — takjub
- **disappointed** — kecewa

Perhatikan perbedaan **-ed** vs **-ing**: *I was bored* (perasaan saya) vs *The film was boring* (sifat filmnya). *I was amazed* vs *The view was amazing*. *-ed* describes how a person feels; *-ing* describes the thing that causes the feeling.

### Reacting to a story
Pendengar yang baik memberi respons singkat: *Really? What happened next? Oh no! What did you do? Thank goodness!* These short reactions show interest and keep the conversation going.

### Eventually, in the end, at the end
*Eventually* and *in the end* both mean "after a long time or after many problems". *At the end* biasanya diikuti *of* dan menunjuk ke bagian akhir sesuatu: *at the end of the film*, *at the end of the street*. So say *In the end, we took a taxi home*, not *At the end, we took a taxi home*.

mistakes.wrong: At the end, we took a taxi home.

mistakes.why: In the end = pada akhirnya; at the end biasanya diikuti of (at the end of the film).

mistakes.wrong: I was very embarrassing when I fell over.
mistakes.right: I was very embarrassed when I fell over.
mistakes.why: Perasaan orang memakai -ed; embarrassing menggambarkan situasinya.

mistakes.why: Kehilangan dompet adalah kabar buruk → unfortunately.

mistakes.right: The film was so boring.
mistakes.why: Sifat film memakai -ing.

sections.summary: A good story has a beginning, a middle and an end. Gunakan connectors seperti **suddenly, luckily, unfortunately, meanwhile, eventually, in the end** untuk memandu pendengar, dan kata sifat emosi seperti **relieved, embarrassed, terrified** untuk menunjukkan perasaan. Remember: *-ed* for feelings, *-ing* for the cause.

questions.prompt: Tell a short story (5–7 sentences) about a day when something unexpected happened to you. Describe the background, the main events, and how you felt.
questions.instructions: Gunakan past continuous untuk latar, past simple untuk kejadian utama, past perfect untuk kejadian sebelumnya, dan minimal dua connectors.
questions.sampleAnswer: Last year I was travelling to Port Selwyn by train. It was raining and I was reading a book. Suddenly, I realised that I had left my bag on the platform. I was terrified because my laptop was in it. Luckily, a station worker found it and sent it on the next train. In the end, I got it back the same evening, and I was so relieved.
questions.explanation: Cerita yang baik memiliki latar (*was travelling, was raining*), kejadian utama (*realised, found*), kejadian sebelumnya (*had left*), connectors, dan perasaan.
